This study uses around 40 picobarns of data collected by the D0 detector at the Tevatron to experimentally measure the decay time of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ meson system. Our measurement, where we account for background, yields a result of 1.459 picoseconds with a margin of error of 0.026 picoseconds. This result differs from theoretical predictions made using the Standard Model of physics, where the same outcome would be 1.480 picoseconds. Although this variation is statistically significant at a 3-sigma level of confidence, further research is needed to determine if it indicates a departure from the predictions made by the Standard Model.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of noise; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an error estimate; this conclusion is verified through computational experiments showing the method's effectiveness.

Our observatory at the Pierre Auger Site utilized 24 circular arrays and 27 long baselines to monitor cosmic rays with energies exceeding 4 EeV, covering a wide sky area of approximately $70^\circ$. Our primary objective was to identify any patterns or deviations in the distribution of cosmic rays originating from the northern and southern hemispheres. Following adjustments for local cosmic ray maxima and surrounding areas, we discovered a significant pattern ($9.1\sigma$) pointing towards the direction of the Galactic Center. This anomaly is statistically robust and persists even after accounting for potential biases. We also found a secondary pattern ($4.5\sigma$) directed towards the opposite side of the Milky Way. This pattern becomes more pronounced when focusing on cosmic rays entering the atmosphere at shallow angles. These discoveries have implications for our current understanding of interactions between high-energy cosmic rays and the intergalactic medium, and may influence the composition and energy spectra of cosmic rays. Furthermore, this finding raises questions about potential sources of cosmic rays and their connections to large-scale structures in the universe.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. This study utilizes a minimum bias selection, incorporating events with transverse neutron energy above 0.1 GeV and 0.05 radians, to report various particle distributions, including spectra, mean pT, and the coefficient of second pT moment, all normalized by the corresponding pp values. The results also convey the ratio of p+Pb to pp mean pT and the second pT moment. Furthermore, this analysis examines the ratio of proton-proton and p+Pb interactions for different centralities, revealing a nuclear modification factor (NP) that fluctuates between -0.20 and 0.20, depending on charged particle count.

This paper introduces a quantum mechanical system defined by a noncommutative version of a given Lie algebra, specifically focusing on the su(2) and sl(2) algebras. We then derive the corresponding Hamiltonians and discuss their equivalence in both commutative and noncommutative contexts. Additionally, we examine the deformation of these algebras and its implications for the quantum mechanical systems, including the effects of noncommutativity and deformations on the energy levels and wave functions.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training a convolutional neural network to classify tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes based on their abundance and type. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse data set of 25,000 images, we compared the results of training models in a federated setting to those obtained through centralized learning. The findings showed that models trained in a federated manner were comparable to those trained through centralized learning, with an accuracy of 92% in the private round, indicating that FL is a viable approach for this type of classification.

In this study, a high-speed underwater fiber transmission system uses the 1.25 Gbps 64-QAM signal and reaches a data transfer rate of 10 Gbps. However, the equalization process in this system is hampered by a significant issue known as burst-error propagation, which causes a substantial reduction in its bit error rate and performance. To address this problem, a decision-feedback equalizer-enhanced sparse-canoncial decomposition method was developed and effectively reduced the bit error rate to an acceptable level of 10^-3 in a field trial, proving the technique's efficacy.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal models for a given dataset, one of which serves as the final, fully-pruned model. We've demonstrated the efficacy of our approach on four prominent datasets across three application domains, exceeding the performance of baseline models and rivaling the best dilation strategies.

This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotent. To establish this characteristic, we draw upon the concept of the Grassmann algebra, specifically its exterior powers. By defining the appropriate filtration based on these exterior powers, we demonstrate that the Zinbiel algebra in question becomes a solvable algebra.

Our study offers initial findings on a particular aspect of flow related to collisions between lead ions at the LHC, specifically on the angle and magnitude fluctuations of flow. We analyzed angle fluctuations of flow to establish a connection with the volume fluctuations, while also determining the shear viscosity of the medium. Conversely, magnitude fluctuations of flow reveal information about the initial state of the system in a manner that's sensitive to the details of the fluctuation in the shear stress tensor of the nucleus. However, we weren't able to draw a clear conclusion in this case. We based our analysis on data from the ALICE experiment and corresponding collisions between proton ions at several energies, utilizing data from the AMPT model as a comparison.

In 1990, Alves proposed an inverse theorem for certain types of distributive semvalued lattices known as DLE-Logics, which served as a fundamental basis for further explorations in the field. Notably, his work laid the groundwork for the development of analytic and algebraic techniques in DLE-Logics. However, the original publication of the inverse theorem was initially met with skepticism and eventually the method it employed was deemed unsatisfying. As a result, the theorem and its associated algebraic structure were largely forgotten. This paper aims to revive the interest in the original inverse theorem and has successfully derived a more general version of it, which can be applied to a broader class of distributive semvalued lattices. Moreover, the paper also explores the underlying properties of the distributivity operation within these lattices, specifically addressing the conditions under which the inverse theorem holds true.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. When a data entry is missing, it is denoted by a null, and the paper's authors aim to go beyond conventional approaches by also considering the inherent connections between data fields, often referred to as functional dependencies. The authors propose a framework that combines nulls and functional dependencies to model inconsistencies and incorporate a set of rules that can be used for resolution purposes. Their method allows for the identification of potential solutions to data entry issues, and it also enables finding minimal answers to resolved problems. The paper's authors demonstrate that their approach outperforms existing methods in terms of efficiency and present case studies to illustrate the practical applications of their method.

This study presents a novel dynamic model called Poisson autoregressive (PAR) model that incorporates time-varying characteristics for counting data. Our model proceeds by introducing a dynamic framework that allows for changes in parameters over time, thereby generating time-dependent conditional Poisson distributions. This approach is mathematically expressed as a state space model, enabling the retrieval of forecast probabilities at any point in the past or future with a high degree of accuracy. Notably, our model offers an effective method for predicting rare events. Another significant benefit is derived from the state space framework, providing consistent estimates of model parameters. These estimates, in turn, enable the computation of key metrics such as entropy, thus offering valuable insights into the model's behavior. Our model's performance is evaluated against current techniques, revealing improved forecasting capabilities and a greater ability to capture the time-varying nature of counting data.

Objects in an scene can be described using various features such as color, depth, and normals. Our proposal, Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), uses a neural network to create a object representation that is both SE(3)-equivariant and detailed. This representation is then used for an object detection task in a scene. We experimentally show that NDFs lead to a significant improvement in detection accuracy when compared to other descriptor-based methods. Furthermore, NDFs are highly versatile and can be combined with traditional detection methods, resulting in an even higher boost in performance. We have released our code along with demonstration videos at https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~daviddu6/neural-descriptor-fields.html.

The SiD Detector is one of the four detector designs proposed to search for the source of new physics with the ILC. Given that the ILC's parameters can be adjusted, we are re-examining the SiD's design with a focus on optimized performance in certain areas, particularly on the transition magnetic field and the calorimeter's central region. Additionally, we are incorporating two new features: a Mollenauer scanner for measuring bolt patterns in the silicon vertices, and a Drell-Yan process for controlling closure gaps in the central calorimeter.

We performed a detailed analysis of the globular cluster Tononzintla 2. Members of this cluster were identified through CAPOS data, within a $3.5^\circ$ field centered on Tonzintla 2, by combining CAPOS photometry with a spectroscopic imaging technique using APOGEE data. We removed extractions that contained more than one APOGEE target or were taken in the direction of the galaxy's major axis, resulting in the removal of 275, or 12.1%, of ca-POS data, and 1,025, or 34.5%, of the ca-SPOS data. This approach left 1,945 cluster members in 1,025 ca-POS data, and 1,975 cluster members in 1,975 ca-SPOS data. We used these members to determine a more precise cluster motion, and estimate a cluster distance of 16.3 $\pm$ 1.8 parsecs, consistent with estimates from the CAPOS data alone, and 28.1 $\pm$ 3.9 km/s, both in the plane and perpendicular to the plane of the sky. This cluster's motion is distinct from that of the nearby cluster Tonzintla 1. We used the ca-SPOS data to determine a more precise mass-loss rate for this cluster, estimating it to be $\dot{M}_* \approx 0.31\pm 0.15 M_\

Formal verification uses proof representations to validate theories and programs, confirming their correctness and functional behavior as expected.  The Isabelle theorem prover has a growing repository of documented proofs available for examination, providing valuable insights into its capabilities and any limitations encountered during the proof-making process.  This study presents an comprehensive analysis of this repository, focusing on the underlying structure and efficiency of the proofs presented, with the aim of identifying best practices and areas for improvement in the theorem prover.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and physics, the first step in analyzing approximate message passing (AMP) messages often yields a simplified set of equations that mirror the symmetries of the original problem. We investigated these simplified messages in various contexts, deriving their properties and relationships. We expressed the messages as a function of the parabolic approximation of the target function, and demonstrated that these messages convey valuable information about the geometry of the target function. We utilized this understanding to verify the curvature results obtained through the wet lemma of the extended generalized approximate message passing (xGAMP) algorithm. Our findings can be applied to a broad category of problems, including those with unique minima, where the geometry of the target function can be analyzed using the curvature result.

Recent advancements in nanotechnology and electromagnetic theory have enabled the design of controllable electromagnetic fields through spatially localized concepts, specifically quasi-conjugate surface interactions. This research focuses on the interface between a perfect electric conductor and a planar perfect magnetic conductor, which it applies to develop complex electromagnetic field control systems, leveraging microwave circuit components and microfluidic channels to create dynamic systems. A symbolic mathematical approach is proposed for complex field analysis, involving the expansion of electromagnetic wave expressions in terms of plane waves and generalized scattering matrices. Furthermore, this proposal can be extended to study non-conductive metasurfaces, represented by generalized conformal space transformation, and it demonstrates the potential to model various surface configurations using conformal transformations, ultimately enabling the analysis of complex field behavior in conformal surfaces.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth fully integrable vector fields near a compact subset of a smooth manifold. Our proof leverages Ruh's approach, along with additional arguments. We also demonstrate that fully integrable vector fields exhibit key properties, including local stability and global smooth conjugacy to a linear conjugacy. Additionally, we provide an example illustrating that convergent smooth flows are not necessarily fully integrable.

This study investigates the potential of deep learning to capture intricate configuration interaction (CI) electron correlations within full CI calculations, exceeding thousands of dimensions. Our approach, a novel correlation network called the CI Correlation Network (CI-CNet), directly produces a complete set of one-electron density matrices from input spatial electronic densities. This allows it to efficiently derive the full CI wave function and energies for small atomic and molecular systems, with parameters learned from small datasets representing average energies over all possible CIs. Our results show that this deep learning approach can replicate the complexities of certain CI manifolds and generate improved results when applied to limited data sets, potentially enabling the acceleration of time-consuming high-dimensional optimizations required in full CI calculations.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed the "Ring of Fire," spanning approximately 11 million light-years. It is observed to be vacuuming up massive amounts of gas, causing nearby star formation to be suppressed. Additionally, it is reflecting a massive arc of light, making it a potentially remarkable sight from space. Furthermore, due to its massive size, it is likely affecting multiple nearby galaxy formations. We are seeking further observations to better understand its impact on surrounding galaxy formations.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, our method measures the aerosol depth with a precision of 0.01 by accounting for systematic errors and varying conditions. This is because the entire night sky is affected by the same atmospheric conditions, essentially serving as a large number of independent optical depth measurements. Using this approach, we conducted extensive monitoring of the atmospheric conditions at one site over the course of several years, observing minimal variations in the aerosol depth during the day. Our method measures the angular variation of the aerosol depth, potentially providing information on the shape of aerosols, and we discovered a value of approximately 10 degrees. Furthermore, we found that our results are consistent with the spatial coherence of turbulent eddies being controlled by the height, as predicted by the theory of similarity.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using deep learning methods has gained significant interest due to their speed and accuracy. Our proposed network, DeepHMap++, employs a novel two-stage architecture to achieve this goal. In the first stage, the model uses a projection clustering technique called Connected Component Labeling (CCL) to divide a object's 2D projection into distinct regions based on contrast levels. These regions act as local descriptors that correspond to specific areas of the object, thereby making them more robust to changes in light and background. Our model learns these local descriptors and their corresponding 3D poses in a semi-supervised manner. In the second stage, the local descriptors from the first stage are used as input to a correspondence learner that refines the estimates of 6D poses through global optimization. Our experiments demonstrate that DeepHMap++ surpasses the current state-of-the-art models in the LINEMOD and ITOW datasets, showcasing its ability to provide more accurate results. Moreover, our model achieves exceptional performance when tested with the MODAL dataset, a recently released benchmark.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuity formation within materials. Bond-based Peridynamics, having no connection with the theory's name, is a highly versatile approach that has been successfully applied to a wide range of problems involving cracking phenomena and other types of material failure. Despite its numerous successes, BBP is not a derivative of first-order equations; instead, it yields a high-order differential equation that is susceptible to numerical instability during long-time simulations. Various methods have been proposed to mitigate this issue, such as introducing a finite bond length, constructing an ADI algorithm, or utilizing a semi-implicit numerical scheme. Although these methods have shown some promise in extending the validity of the simulations, more research is needed to fully understand their effects on the model's solutions. Furthermore, the PD concept has yet to be thoroughly explored in terms of its noncircovity and radon uniqueness, especially when applied to fluid dynamics.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address a broad spectrum of
Graphical Lasso problems, encompassing various objectives, regularization
strategies, and solver techniques. Initially developed to facilitate the
implementation of scaled $l_1$-penalized Node-wise Graphical Lasso, GGLasso has
evolved into a versatile framework, capable of handling diverse Graphical
Lassoestimation frameworks. Its robust nature allows it to handle large sparse
graphs, facilitated by the PySparse library, and it also supports the use
of the scikit-sparse package for handling sparse matrices. Furthermore, GGLassois adaptable to various processing unit architectures, thanks to its
underlying matrix operation functionality based on NumPy.

A newly developed algorithm for Monte Carlo simulations tackles polynomial threshold functions with a significant advantage over established methods. By leveraging Langevin dynamics, this method efficiently generates desired binary configurations by sampling from a probability distribution aligned with the energy landscape of the Fefferman function. The algorithm's efficacy is particularly evident when it compares to the Fixed-Ferroelectric Algorithm, especially as the number of OR gates increases - whereas the FFA's performance declines with each additional gate, the new algorithm maintains a constant exponential decrease in error. The reason behind this difference in performance is attributed to the varying impact of ferroelectric fluctuations, which affects the accuracy of the FFA.

We simulated black hole mergers within a dark matter halo to study how surrounding matter fields influence gravitational waves. Our framework models dark matter as a smooth, overdense region, while baryons are represented by discrete, collisional objects. We ran over 200 simulations for various dark matter configurations, ranging from simple halos to complex networks, and compared our results to candle models. Our analysis suggests that gravitational wave amplitudes are generally consistent across different dark matter setups, but there are notable differences in waveform morphology. We also observed distinct features in frequency spectra, including characteristic resonances and nonlinearities. Our findings highlight the significance of incorporating dark matter interactions with baryons in order to accurately predict gravitational wave signatures.

We examine the dynamic stability of a pre-curved, elastic beam subjected to a constant external force, taking into account the effects of rotation on the beam's cross-section. To model this scenario, we employ a modified Euler-Bernoulli beam theory that accounts for both curvature and rotation. Our analysis focuses on a star-shaped graph and leverages Lyapunov's indirect method to determine the conditions under which the beam maintains a stable equilibrium configuration. Our findings highlight the importance of the beam's rotation in preventing instability. Notably, our work highlights the challenge of interpreting results through the Lyapunov direct method due to the beam's infinite number of degrees of freedom.

Researchers demonstrated a novel sonic lens material based on rubber-like silicone containing microbursts that significantly enhance the acoustical contrast to facilitate clear image capture. A large format detector with 256 transducers was used to obtain high resolution pictures, showing the effectiveness of this sonic lens material in photoacoustics tomography. A comparison was made with a conventional sonic lens made from copper, the simplest form of sonic lens.  A key advantage of the rubber-like silicone sonic lens is its ability to maximize the photoacoustic signal while preventing the acoustics from the focus from overpowering the system, thus allowing a clearer image.  Notably, breast tumors as small as 1 cm^3 can be detected with this technique.

Our new method calculates a variation of the eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance from related layers. In previous studies, researchers have developed various centrality measurements for analyzing the importance of nodes within individual network layers. However, these approaches fail to consider the connections between different layers in a multilayered network. In contrast, our proposed approach takes into account the interconnected nature of multilayered networks by incorporating node importance from related layers. Specifically, we've developed a new formula for calculating the variation of the eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that accounts for the connected layers. In addition, the algorithm for solving this connected variant converges more quickly than other similar methods.

We tackle the problem of non-blind and blind image denoising, addressing real-world challenges posed by noisy, blurred, and partially occluded images. Unlike traditional approaches that treat these issues in isolation, we propose a novel joint deblurring, demosaicking, and denoising framework capable of leveraging raw image data. Our method first estimates the blurring kernel and demosaicking mask simultaneously, treating them as unknowns, and leverages these predictions to enhance subsequent denoising performance. This framework is particularly effective in processing raw images obtained from cameras under unknown conditions. We evaluate our technique against state-of-the-art techniques for deblurring, demosaicking, and image denoising in a non-blind setting, and also against relevant raw image processing methods in a blind scenario, yielding superior results according to PSNR and SSIM metrics.

We explore how the spacetime curvature affects the energy spectrum of a particle, specifically examining the curvature-induced potential that a charged scalar particle experiences under its influence, as described by the Dirac equation in $R$-Minkowski spacetime. To this end, we derive the equation's exact form and identify its stationary solutions in terms of spinor fields for an arbitrary potential. Furthermore, we determine the energy spectrum and its associated eigenvalues for a harmonic potential. Additionally, we investigate how the curvature impacts energy levels in two notable cases: when the curvature is aligned with the potential, and when it is perpendicular to it.

Intelligent systems consistently face a challenge: exploring their environment to gain insight before taking action, all while navigating limited resources and a complex domain. This difficulty prompts our proposal of a causal learning framework, designed to help these systems efficiently discover causal relationships within their environment. We've developed the Causal Exploration Toolbox (CET), a comprehensive Python library offering versatile methods for identifying causal connections. These methods encompass both model-free approaches, such as active learning and optimal intervention design, and model-dependent strategies, like inverse reinforcement learning and causal structure learning, utilizing established libraries like Gym and MultiAgent-Python. To demonstrate CET's utility, we've included example use cases spanning various domains and problem types, including real-world applications and data sets. We believe CET to be a valuable resource for researchers working on causal exploration and reinforcement learning, as well as developers of autonomous systems, by providing a set of causal relationship discovery tools that can be seamlessly integrated into Python projects.

This study investigates how spheres behave when entering water at medium speeds, specifically focusing on the interaction between the sphere and water's surface tension. Research has already explored two speed extremes: high-speed regimes, characterized by significant water displacement and localized air trapping; and low-speed regimes, marked by substantial water infiltration and seal establishment before significant water displacement occurs. In the medium-speed regime studied here, our results show that spheres create a seal during water entry, yet fail to trap substantial amounts of air. Moreover, we observed that a crucial factor influencing seal performance is the sphere's diameter relative to the depth of water infiltration, which affects water displacement and air trapping. Additionally, our data suggest that the air trapped during water entry is insufficient to prevent water infiltration, thus leading to partial seal establishment and subsequent water displacement. A new theoretical model is proposed to explain these phenomena, involving the interplay between water pressure, surface tension, and air pressure within the trapped volume.

We investigate a class of Type IIB compactifications that feature a generalized symmetry under two dimensions, which is encapsulated in the structure of a semi-simple algebra. Focusing on the effective four-dimensional theory, we find that this symmetry can be expressed through a set of complex scalar fields associated with the higher-dimensional gauge potentials. These scalar fields are linked to the complexified Kähler moduli of the complexified Calabi-Yau manifold that arises when the Type IIB theory is combined with Type IIA theory. We also show that the generalized symmetry can be broken at a fundamental level, resulting in the generation of complex generalized theta-terms within the four-dimensional effective theory. This phenomenon is connected to the presence of a non-zero NSNS flux within the higher-dimensional theory. We then establish the relationship between the generalized symmetry-breaking and the generation of a complex generalized Chern-Simons term in the four-dimensional effective theory. This relationship is dependent on the orientation of the M5-branes in the higher-dimensional theory. Furthermore, we find that the generalized symmetry-breaking leads to a complex generalization of the prepotential that arises within the four-dimensional effective theory. This complex prepotential contains both the prepotential associated with the real part of the complexified Kähler moduli and the prepotential linked to the complex structure moduli. We outline the components necessary for a complete description of the four-dimensional effective theory.

Mobile devices, especially smartphones and tablets, contain sensitive information that could fall prey to malicious software and hardware attacks. The statistics show that a significant portion of Android devices are vulnerable to malware and side-channel attacks. To protect data confidentiality, we introduce a novel approach, 'Physically Isolated Hardware Module' (PIHM), combining hardware isolation and minimal hardware usage to decrease trust in PIHMs. We design a hardware module, 'Physically Isolated Hardware Box' (PIHB), consisting of a separate hardware cavity within a larger device frame. It utilizes a hardware component that, due to its size, cannot fit in the device's regular PCB, thus minimizing the attack surface and trust in the hardware. To increase efficiency, we propose a layering hardware architecture, 'Multi-PIH Layered Architecture' (MPA), utilizing multiple small-sized hardware components to perform different tasks simultaneously, while they are being used for other purposes, reducing the need for physical hardware modifications and resulting in lower costs and faster deployment. To demonstrate the feasibility of our approach, we build a working prototype and conduct a performance evaluation of the MPA, showing it can deliver satisfactory performance in various applications. To further decrease trust in the hardware, we design a 'Hardware Component Multi-PIHM' (HCMPIHM) system, utilizing a small hardware component that can be replaced frequently, while the device's regular hardware component remains the same, reducing the attack window and increasing the trust in the hardware over time. Reinforcement learning (RL) is widely used to optimize complex systems, but it can be challenging to achieve high efficiency when experiencing significant data losses. In this research, we discover a powerful RL policy gradient that resists data corruption and can be stable even with strong contamination, and we demonstrate its optimal performance in various difficult situations. Additionally, we find a key factor that contributes to its robustness and counterintuitive efficiency, and we confirm the accuracy of our analysis through multiple random simulations. Our findings provide valuable insights for designing and optimizing RL algorithms in sensitive environments.

We uncover a variant of the well-known box game paradox, featuring players making choices simultaneously, without prior knowledge of each other's actions. A key aspect of this paradox is that one player's optimal strategy relies on the assumption that the other player is acting randomly, yet this condition is not essential for achieving the desired outcome.

Our investigation of cubanite, with strong spin-orbit coupling and double exchange interactions, challenges the widely held notion that a large effective exchange interaction alone can't cause orbital selection in the ground state.  Our results show that the ground state of cubanite is an anti-ferromagnetically ordered state with differently aligned spins for different $d$-orbitals,  a phenomenon we attribute to the interplay of double and heisenberg exchange interactions.  We further predict that application of a light-matter field should enable orbital discrimination.  We suggest that angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy hold the key to experimentally confirming our theoretical predictions.

A promising approach to enhancing the quantum characteristics of light-matter interactions involves combining systems with large Rabi oscillations and extreme energy shifts. However, controlling Rabi oscillations in semiconductors is challenging due to the rapid decay of quantum coherence. This concept faces an even greater obstacle in semiconductor quantum dots, specifically the dark exciton, which presents a complex control issue. This paper discusses an unprecedented breakthrough where massive Rabi oscillations in the dark exciton were achieved without the use of an external magnetic field. This achievement was made possible by carefully selecting a quantum well with a unique structure, specifically one that allows for spatially separated electron and hole spins as a result of lateral confinement. Additionally, researchers were able to successfully modulate the dark exciton's Rabi oscillations by adjusting an applied electric field, which induced a magnetic field in the dot. This resulted in an astonishing 100 MHz frequency modulation. This groundbreaking method may pave the way for the development of complex quantum dot systems that could potentially achieve large-scale quantum coherent phenomena.

Our investigation reveals a novel 2D non-symmorphic wallpaper network lattice that supports three distinct types of propagating modes, which can be described using the tight-binding model. We demonstrated that this lattice exhibits tunable Dirac points by means of a close-packed honeycomb hidden structure within its unit cell. We utilized the Fermi surface concept to illustrate the existence of these hidden structures and showed that the band structure can be modified to yield tunable Dirac points. We also demonstrated that this lattice enables quasi-long-range-order phenomena and investigated the effects of lattice defects on the hidden structure and band structure. Notably, this lattice allows for the coexistence of a insulating state and a QLRO state by means of the hidden structure.

We investigate a novel coherent state transformation made possible by a single-photon catalysis process between modes A and B. A unitary transformation, facilitated by the action of beam splitters BS1 and BS2, achieves this transformation. Our analysis reveals that certain coherent states in mode A, following this process, will result in specific phases appearing in the correlation function of mode B. This phenomenon doesn't occur in conventional catalysis processes using multi-photon catalysis. Our research also shows that this single-photon catalysis process can create a range of coherent states with distinct phases. This feature might be utilized in the development of all-optical catalysis-based phase modulators capable of producing various coherent states with specific phases.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying electromagnetic fields and the Ricci tensors. This review focuses on the fundamental principles of the formalism, detailing how the bivectors are defined and their physical implications. It also explores finding the Ricci coefficients, discussing various methods including the direct determination of the conformal curvature class of a spacetime.

A recent approach combining artificial neural networks and mixed-integer linear programming has shown significant potential in synthesizing polymer structures from mass spectrometry data. However, this method's limitation in using only a single variable for each monomer type restricts its applicability to certain scenarios. As an alternative, we've developed a new method utilizing linear regression and mixed-integer linear programming for polymer identification. This technique leverages linear regression to estimate a broad range of potential polymer formulas based on mass spectrometry data and then employs an artificial neural network within an integer programming framework to refine these estimates. The linear regression step's ability to handle multiple variables for each monomer type enhances the method's ability to accurately recover polymers. Furthermore, the proposed technique demonstrates improved performance compared to existing approaches using the same data from previous studies.

Optimizing control systems for continuous processes through reinforcement learning and other model-free methods can be challenging and expensive due to the need for process models. This paper explores an alternative approach called direct transcription, an optimization method that uses smooth functions to approximate the behavior of the process over time. This approach involves setting up a mathematical model that describes the process dynamics and uses state feedback control. The process is then optimized by adjusting the control inputs to minimize errors or achieve a desired outcome. We will review the steps involved in the direct transcription optimization method, including the development of process models, integration of differential equations, and formulation of objective functions for optimization. The paper will provide a case study on the optimization of a dual-patient ventilation system during the COVID-19 pandemic, where there was a critical shortage of ventilators in the intensive care unit (ICU). The study aimed to increase the capacity of a single ventilator by ventilating two patients simultaneously, while ensuring the safety and effectiveness of the treatment. The paper will outline the development of a process model for the dual-patient ventilation system, including the formulation of an objective function for optimization, and present the results of direct transcription optimization, including the code used. The study demonstrated a 25% increase in the survival rate of COVID-19 patients on ventilators by optimizing the control inputs of the ventilation system. The paper will provide a code example for the optimization of the dual-patient ventilation system, which can be modified for the optimization of other continuous processes.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other diagnostic tools during cancer treatment planning. However, this process can be time-consuming and may slow down treatment progression. To streamline this process, a more accurate and efficient automatic system for detecting tumors in the esophagus from CT scans is presented here. This system, inspired by recent advancements in automatic cardiac segmentation, is designed to automatically identify and outline tumors in the esophagus from CT scans with high precision. To account for the limited contrast of these scans, a new type of neural network called the Dilated Dense Focus AUNet (DDAUNet) is developed, offering enhanced performance compared to existing alternatives. To train this network and ensure it can be applied to any hospital or be used by any researcher, a large dataset of 1024 times thicker CT slices is used, comprising over 2000 scans with outlined tumors. To test this system's accuracy, a smaller independent set of 200 scans with outlined tumors is used, showing that it can detect tumors with high precision and low error, outperforming existing competitors.

The expense associated with drilling offshore wells is significant and can add millions to the cost of each hole. Describing the subsurface formation accurately while drilling, a process known as geosteering, is crucial to avoid costly missteps. This geosteering process can be achieved by combining the data from drilling and logging operations in real-time, thus enabling data-driven decision making. A novel approach to modeling the uncertainty of formation properties using a batch ensemble method and a kernel-based similarity measure for data completion is presented in this study. This approach is demonstrated on a real-data scenario where it yields a comparative analysis of the proposed method against existing techniques. The results show that the proposed method delivers a precise and efficient formation property model, outperforming rival methods. This approach is subsequently applied to an complex real-world problem involving geosteering.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which fail to capture the inherent hierarchical nature of nested entities. In contrast, we propose integrating nested NER into a parsing framework that addresses all linguistic structures, including hierarchical entities. A nested entity is considered a specific type of syntactic structure comprising multiple other structures, each representing a single entity. We leverage a Japanese corpus to demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, using a robust model that accurately identifies all entities within a sentence.

We provide a counting of signed roots for a specific class of objects - plane quartics with a tangent condition - in relation to their bi-tangents, giving an explicit formula involving the Euler characteristic of moduli spaces of tropical curves. Additionally, we establish the rationality of certain spaces related to these objects. Furthermore, we offer an alternative interpretation of the count of these objects in relation to bi-tangents via geometric $\mathbb{A}^1$-localization.

Research into the localization of wireless devices within a sensor network is currently being conducted, with the aim of enhancing various applications, including positioning, vehicle tracking, and environmental monitoring. This work investigates the challenge of accurately determining the position of a target device in a network, whose components operate on the IEEE 802.15.1 (Bluetooth) standard, is subject to interference from other technologies, and has limited cooperation with nearby nodes. To overcome these obstacles, a new method, known as the Standard Reference Device Method, has been developed. The scheme's effectiveness was demonstrated in a simulated environment using devices based on the TelosB platform, with the target device's position being determined using three reference devices, located at standard distances from it, to create a triangular coordinate system. The results show that the method can provide accurate location estimates, with an average error of less than a metre.

Code-mixing, the practice of speaking two or more languages within a single conversation, is a common communication approach used extensively across various social media platforms. This paper delves into the complexities of NLP systems that handle these code-mixed conversations in three key areas: sentiment analysis, language-specific task, and code-mixed task. Although substantial progress has been made in NLP research that addresses single-language challenges, there is a significant gap in code-ming NLP. To illustrate this disparity, the paper presents initial experiments on three sentiment analysis tasks conducted in multiple languages. The results indicate that NLP systems perform notably worse when dealing with code-ming data compared to solely monolingual data. Several factors contribute to this difficulty, including the need for NLP systems to be multilingual, the issue of data scarcity, and the presence of linguistic nuances that are unique to code-ming. Moreover, the paper discusses several challenges that code-ming NLP systems face, such as determining the language of each word within the code-ming sentence, dealing with the complex linguistic structure of code-ming, and addressing the issue of dataset bias. To overcome these obstacles, several approaches have been proposed, including the use of character-based models, BERT-based multilingual models, and data augmentation techniques. Nonetheless, a considerable amount of work remains to be done in order to develop effective NLP systems that can efficiently handle code-ming data.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to evaluate visual description generation systems. However, it's often assumed that these descriptions are more accurate than the system's output, which is not necessarily true. We analyzed a popular benchmark dataset, Flickr30k, consisting of human descriptions, and found it flawed for system evaluation. Specifically, we discovered that the existing dataset is not suitable for rigorous, systematic testing. We explained the underlying issues causing these problems and suggested alternative, higher-quality datasets for accurately assessing the performance of visual description generation systems.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and thermal stability. To understand their electronic behavior, computational models employed two methods: first, a theoretical prediction based on fundamental properties, and second, a statistical simulation modeling different crystalline structures. The predicted model, derived from fundamental properties, indicated that Ta$_2$O$_5$ has a complex structure with multiple forms, but the statistical simulation, modeling the actual physical conditions, produced results closely matching those of the predicted model, particularly in terms of optical and dielectric characteristics. Furthermore, the results suggested that Ta$_2$O$_5$ has potential as a thermoelectric material, but this would require further experimental verification.

We investigated the spread of misinformation on Reddit in the United States in conjunction with the significant geographic shift of users from urban to rural areas that occurred in 2020. We utilized a dataset consisting of 527 million posts and 50 million users, defining misinformation based on the dissemination of debunked information related to four topics: vaccines, climate change, elections, and health. Our analysis revealed a circulation of misinformation among Reddit users increased following the significant shift, especially in rural areas. It also showed that the boost in misinformation circulation held true for all four topics, but the enhancement was more pronounced in urban areas for the topic of climate change. Furthermore, circulation of the same misinformation varied significantly between rural and urban areas over time, as evidenced by minimal overlap in their waveforms. Additionally, our results demonstrated that the circulation of misinformation was higher in rural areas during peak despread periods and that the shift in user geography led to increased circulation in urban areas during peak spread periods. We used subreddits with content related to science, health, and fact-checking to investigate potential explanations and found that the circulation of misinformation could have been impeded by urban users' greater engagement with these types of content. We used additional data to explore potential causal mechanisms and found that the shift in user geography led to increased circulation of misinformation due in part to the influence of rural users on adjacent users in the subreddit waveform.

We introduce a groundbreaking, real-time incident detection system that can
identify anomalies in streaming data. This system leverages a novel approach to
incorporate time-to-detect and other operational constraints into predictive models.
To achieve this, we've developed a mathematical framework that transforms the
incident detection problem into a series of optimization tasks. These optimization
problems can be solved efficiently for small datasets, but they become more complex
when dealing with large datasets. To address this challenge, we've an adaptive
solution that can handle large datasets in real-time by dividing them into smaller
segments. We've tested our approach using a dataset of suspicious financial
transactions and found that it outperforms a existing incident detection system
in terms of detection quality.

To evaluate our approach, we've developed a system that can detect incidents in
real-time and compared it to a state-of-the-art machine learning algorithm. We've
identified several benefits of our approach, including the ability to incorporate
human expertise and a more efficient use of computational resources. We've also
defined several metrics to measure the performance of our system, including its
ability to detect incidents on time and its accuracy.

We've applied our approach to a real-world dataset of suspicious financial
transactions. We've tested our approach using a dataset of financial transactions
